Q [L2]: How did the refund system default to Policy v1’s 30-day window after Policy v2’s 14-day window took effect on 2026-10-18, and what real-time guardrail failed to prevent it?  
Q [L3]: Of the 40 refunds totaling 69,422 EGP, how many orders were delivered 15–29 days pre-incident, and what is the process for remedying customers whose refunds were processed outside the live 14-day window?  
Q [L4]: Why did every agent refund reason explicitly reference the expired 30-day window 34 times, and what automated or supervisory check allowed this systematic policy evasion?

A: The system defaulted to Policy v1's 30-day window because the AI agent was prompted with v1's refund terms (B1) and consistently cited the 30-day window in its decisions (B2), while no real-time guardrail enforced the live v2 14-day policy after its 2026-10-18 effective date. [L2, A1, B1, B2]

A: All 40 of the refunded orders were delivered 15–29 days before the incident, exceeding the live 14-day return window, but the ledger does not document a remediation process for customers refunded outside the policy window. [L3, A2]

A: The ledger and evidence record the refund reasons and policy mismatch but do not explain why agents consistently referenced the expired 30-day window or what automated/supervisory checks permitted this systematic evasion. []
